invariants.description: Synthetic RP ID and origin remain the fixed test pair.
invariants.threat: Caller-controlled origin/RP values being mistaken for trusted application identity.
invariants.limitations: Fixture validation does not prove a real browser origin or application identity.

invariants.description: Credential identities are canonical, bounded and exact.
invariants.threat: Credential aliasing, malformed IDs and unsafe cleanup targets.
invariants.limitations: IDs and inventory are synthetic and do not establish OS credential identity.

invariants.description: Ambiguous inventory changes cannot resolve unknown enrollment or authorize deletion.
invariants.threat: Attributing a pre-existing or unexpected credential to an interrupted operation.
invariants.limitations: The fake inventory is not a real authenticator inventory.

invariants.description: Enrollment collisions and unbound IDs never become trusted or deletable credentials.
invariants.threat: Deleting or pinning a pre-existing credential after a registration collision.
invariants.limitations: Synthetic adapter provenance is not OS attestation.

invariants.description: Interrupted or unknown enrollment and cleanup outcomes remain blocked pending reconciliation.
invariants.threat: Treating response loss, cancellation or unknown operation outcome as success.
invariants.limitations: Reconciliation uses only deterministic fake inventory.

invariants.description: Pinned synthetic trust is revoked before cleanup and stale results cannot restore it.
invariants.threat: Using a credential after cleanup begins or after an ambiguous deletion.
invariants.limitations: Revocation is in-memory fake state, not a persistent production revocation service.

invariants.description: Revocation is irreversible for the same synthetic credential lifecycle.
invariants.threat: Stale journal or cleanup results restoring prior credential trust.
invariants.limitations: The simulation does not model durable multi-process authority state.

invariants.description: Journal transitions are validated by both workflow journal and storage boundary.
invariants.threat: Forged continuation or invalid operation/outcome transitions.
invariants.limitations: Tests exercise an in-memory store simulation.

invariants.description: Journal revisions and operation sequence continuity cannot regress.
invariants.threat: Stale writes, duplicate operations and rollback snapshots.
invariants.limitations: In-memory simulation is not durable or tamper resistant.

invariants.description: Lost or replaced replay ledger continuity blocks further nonce consumption.
invariants.threat: Replaying a previously consumed synthetic challenge after ledger replacement.
invariants.limitations: Does not provide replay protection across real OS process restarts.

invariants.description: Unanchored snapshots cannot fabricate later journal state.
invariants.threat: Restoring a forged terminal snapshot without established history.
invariants.limitations: Genesis validation does not make the in-memory journal authenticated.

invariants.description: Synthetic evidence dimensions must be complete, linked and fixture-sourced.
invariants.threat: Caller metadata or contradictory fixture labels being treated as identity proof.
invariants.limitations: Synthetic consistency is not application attestation or user approval.

invariants.description: Readiness reports are informational and real operations remain blocked.
invariants.threat: Unknown or synthetic readiness being promoted to real credential capability.
invariants.limitations: A static manifest is policy data and cannot establish runtime readiness.

invariants.description: The synthetic lab exposes no live native credential operation.
invariants.threat: Fake lab accidentally invoking a real WebAuthn ceremony or credential API.
invariants.limitations: Source boundary review is not a binary attestation or runtime sandbox.

invariants.description: Experimental state cannot create production authorization or dispatch authority.
invariants.threat: Synthetic trust, mock approval or readiness results reaching production dispatch.
invariants.limitations: Offline verifier output is observational and not a production authorization input.
